---
title: "TRAVELLERS: Travellers"
description: "Information about people who have travelled in or out of Australia."
---

Information about people who have travelled in or out of Australia.

*Defines overseas movement records, traveller types, counting units and related caveats.*

The year opens a Census year, and PP_CENSUS_2016 later in the table carries the status for Census night, 9 August 2016.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia (article, released 18 June 2026)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2016m1","k":"Physically present in Australia status at 31 January 2016","def":"One person's presence flag at 31 January 2016, read as a state at that instant and not as a tally of days spent in the country during January 2016. The classification is physical presence in Australia as the ABS defines it, derived from border movement records, and distinct from the residence rules used to compile the estimated resident population. It opens the 2016 block within a 240-column panel that runs from January 2006 to December 2025, seven months ahead of PP_CENSUS_2016.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia (article, released 18 June 2026)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"Pooling this column with other month ends treats the seasons as interchangeable. The ABS notes that the present population fluctuates more where seasonal factors such as school holidays or annual events bear on it, so a 31 January 2016 reading is not a stand-in for a typical month. PP_CENSUS_2016 arrives seven months later and is the nearest Census-night check.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2016M10","d":"The physically present flag at 31 October 2016, one of the mid-quarter months this panel covers and the ERP table does not.","full":"The physically present flag at 31 October 2016, one of the mid-quarter months this panel covers and the ERP table does not. October is a shoulder month for Australian travel, between the winter outbound season and the summer visitor peak, so the present and resident populations sit close together at this month end. Read along a row from this column and you get one person's presence sequence; read down the column and you get a cross-section of everyone in the country that night.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2016m10","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of October 2016","def":"Per person, one code for 31 October 2016, a mid-quarter month end that only this panel observes. The panel is complete by construction, so a value exists for every person on the migration table whether or not they had any border activity in 2016.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"A not-present value can mean the person had never yet entered Australia, which is a different thing from having left. Anyone whose first border crossing came after October 2016 carries the same reading here as a long-term resident who was overseas that night, and only the earlier columns in the row distinguish them.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2016M11","d":"Presence in Australia at 30 November 2016, the month before the summer peak that this panel records every December.","full":"Presence in Australia at 30 November 2016, the month before the summer peak that this panel records every December. November sits at the start of the visitor build-up, so the December column that follows usually shows a larger present population over the same set of people. As with every column here the status is an ABS derivation from movement records rather than anything a traveller wrote on a card.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2016m11","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of November 2016","def":"A status for 30 November 2016 whose weight, PP_WT_2016M11, is held on a separate table rather than beside it. The status and weight tables carry the same 240 monthly reference dates and are joined on SYNTHETIC_AEUID.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"It cannot show turnover inside the month. Two people with the same November 2016 value may have had entirely different months, one never leaving the country and the other making three trips that all closed before 30 November, and no aggregate built from this column will notice the difference.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2016M12","d":"In-Australia status at 31 December 2016, a quarter end falling at the peak of the southern summer travel season.","full":"In-Australia status at 31 December 2016, a quarter end falling at the peak of the southern summer travel season. December is where presence and residence pull furthest apart, and ABS says so directly: \"The population usually resident is less influenced by seasonality and is usually slightly higher than the population present\" (ABS, Population physically present in Australia). At this month end the country holds a large stock of overseas visitors and is missing a large number of residents on holiday, and both effects land in this single column.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2016m12","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of December 2016","def":"A month-end status for 31 December 2016, the December quarter end that ERP_STATUS_2016Q4 also covers. The two columns answer different questions about the same night and are produced by different ABS processes from a shared set of movement records.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"A December present count is not a December population. Using it as one carries the whole summer swing in visitors and in residents abroad into the estimate, which is the seasonality ERP_STATUS_2016Q4 is built to remove, so December columns are the worst months in the panel to use as a stand-in for population.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2016M2","d":"Whether the person was inside Australia at the end of February 2016, which in that leap year is the night of 29 February.","full":"Whether the person was inside Australia at the end of February 2016, which in that leap year is the night of 29 February. This is one column of a monthly panel, so a person's presence history runs left to right across the 240 PP_STATUS columns rather than down the rows, and a single row is one person's whole travel-derived timeline from 2006 onwards. February 2016 sits in the ordinary pre-pandemic pattern, at the tail of the southern summer when returning residents and departing visitors both unwind the January peak.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2016m2","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of February 2016","def":"A categorical status for one person at one month end, 29 February 2016, and not a count, a duration or a date. It is column 122 of the 240 PP_STATUS columns that run from 2006M1 to 2025M12 on a table holding one row per person keyed by SYNTHETIC_AEUID. PLIDA publishes no valid-response list for the item, so the categories in the extract have to be tabulated before use.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"A month-end reading says nothing about the days in between. Somebody who flew out on 3 February 2016 and landed back on 27 February reads the same as somebody who never left, while a two-week trip straddling 29 February reads as away for the whole month. To see a trip you need the arrival and departure rows in the yearly travellers tables, not this panel.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2016M3","d":"The person's in-Australia status at 31 March 2016, the one month in that quarter which lines up with ERP_STATUS_2016Q1.","full":"The person's in-Australia status at 31 March 2016, the one month in that quarter which lines up with ERP_STATUS_2016Q1. Presence and residence are different questions and the ABS builds the aggregate from both: \"Physically present population estimates (PPPE) are calculated as ERP plus total Visitors Temporarily in Australia (VTA) less total Residents Temporarily Overseas (RTO)\" (ABS, Population physically present in Australia). A tourist in the country on 31 March 2016 is present but not resident, and an Australian working overseas that month is resident but not present.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2016m3","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of March 2016","def":"One code per person for 31 March 2016, one of the four month ends a year that share a reference date with the quarterly residence table, here ERP_STATUS_2016Q1 in madipge_mig_d_erp_2006_current. ABS assigns the value by sequencing Home Affairs arrival and departure records into a movement history, which makes it a statistical determination rather than a traveller declaration.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"It cannot tell you who was an Australian resident. Treating a present flag as membership of the estimated resident population counts in visitors who were only passing through and drops residents who happened to be abroad on 31 March 2016, which is exactly the correction ERP_STATUS_2016Q1 in madipge_mig_d_erp_2006_current exists to make.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2016M4","d":"Presence in Australia at 30 April 2016, a month end with no counterpart in the quarterly ERP table.","full":"Presence in Australia at 30 April 2016, a month end with no counterpart in the quarterly ERP table. The monthly grid is the finer of the two: ERP_STATUS exists only at quarter ends, so January, February, April, May, July, August, October and November all have a presence reading and no residence reading at all. April 2016 is an unremarkable month for Australian travel, which makes it a useful baseline against the disrupted months of 2020 further along the same panel.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2016m4","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of April 2016","def":"The item holds a location status for the 30 April 2016 month end, one of the eight months a year the presence panel covers and the quarterly residence table does not. Its matching weight is PP_WT_2016M4 in madipge_mig_d_ppw_2006_current; the status table carries no weight of its own, so tallies taken straight off it are unweighted record counts.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"You cannot read a length of stay off one column. Months in the country across 2016 have to be counted over the twelve PP_STATUS columns for that year, and the answer is then a count of month ends rather than of days, so a person who spent 29 days of April overseas and 29 days of May overseas can still show as present at both month ends.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2016M5","d":"The physically present flag for 31 May 2016, worked out from the person's sequenced border movements.","full":"The physically present flag for 31 May 2016, worked out from the person's sequenced border movements. May is a quiet month for arrivals into Australia, so the present and resident populations sit about as close together as they get in a pre-pandemic year. The status is derived rather than declared: nothing on an incoming passenger card says physically present, and ABS reaches the value by ordering the arrival and departure records it holds for that person.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2016m5","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of May 2016","def":"A per-person value for 31 May 2016 held on a wide table: 240 monthly PP_STATUS columns, four PP_CENSUS columns and the SYNTHETIC_AEUID key, 245 fields in all. Reading it means reading one cell of that rectangle, and the item has no published code list to read it against.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","lim":"It cannot separate somebody who never left Australia from somebody whose crossings the movement file did not capture. A person with no border record generates no movement history to sequence, so an unbroken run of identical values across 2016 may reflect a settled life or may reflect thin coverage, and the column carries nothing that tells the two apart.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2016M6","d":"In-Australia status at 30 June 2016, both a quarter end and a financial year end, matching ERP_STATUS_2016Q2.","full":"In-Australia status at 30 June 2016, both a quarter end and a financial year end, matching ERP_STATUS_2016Q2. The residence measure beside it rests on a different concept: ABS states that \"The official measure of the population of Australia is based on the concept of usual residence\" (ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24). Presence at 30 June 2016 is about where a person physically was on one night, while usual residence is about where they live, and a June financial year end makes this the month most often used to anchor annual measures.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2016m6","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of June 2016","def":"A status for 30 June 2016, the month end that closes both the June quarter and the 2015-16 financial year, and the one paired with ERP_STATUS_2016Q2. The value describes that night alone; the duration measures ABS builds from the same movement records are held in the yearly traveller tables rather than here.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","lim":"Counting the people flagged present at 30 June 2016 does not reproduce any published ABS figure. The panel is unweighted, PP_WT_2016M6 in madipge_mig_d_ppw_2006_current carries the weight for that month, and a raw tally of linked records will sit below the published population present by whatever the weights are there to correct.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2016M7","d":"The presence flag for 31 July 2016, sitting between the June quarter end and the August Census month.","full":"The presence flag for 31 July 2016, sitting between the June quarter end and the August Census month. July opens the financial year and the winter school holidays, so it carries an outward flow of residents that the Census reading a month later does not. As a mid-quarter month it has no ERP counterpart, which makes this column the only statement the migration module makes about where the person was at the end of July 2016.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2016m7","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of July 2016","def":"A location status for 31 July 2016, the first month end of the 2016-17 financial year in this panel. ABS derives it from arrival and departure records supplied by Home Affairs, and no PLIDA product records a traveller stating whether they were in the country that night.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","lim":"An away reading here is not an emigration. Migration in this asset turns on the 12/16 month rule, so one absent month end, or a run of them, is a trip until the cumulative duration test is met, and a July departure for a six-week holiday looks the same in this column as the first month of a permanent move.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2016M8","d":"Presence in Australia at 31 August 2016, three weeks after the Census night that this same table flags in PP_CENSUS_2016.","full":"Presence in Australia at 31 August 2016, three weeks after the Census night that this same table flags in PP_CENSUS_2016. The two columns ask the same question on different nights, and the Census one is anchored to the enumeration concept: \"The place of enumeration is the place at which the person is counted i.e. where he/she spent Census night, which may not be where he/she usually lives\" (ABS Census Dictionary, 2016). Census night was 9 August 2016, so a visitor who flew home mid-month is present in PP_CENSUS_2016 and absent here.","dsrc":"ABS, Census of Population and Housing: Census Dictionary, 2016, Place of Enumeration","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter47002016","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2016m8","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of August 2016","def":"A month-end status for 31 August 2016, sitting on the same table as PP_CENSUS_2016, which flags presence on Census night, 9 August 2016. The two are separate columns with separate reference dates, and neither is derived from the other.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Census of Population and Housing: Census Dictionary, 2016, Place of Enumeration","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter47002016","lim":"It is not the Census reading and will not reconcile with Census counts. Anyone linking this panel to 2016 Census records has to use PP_CENSUS_2016 instead, because 22 days of arrivals and departures separate 9 August from 31 August 2016 and the two columns disagree for every traveller who moved in between.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2016M9","d":"The person's in-Australia status at 30 September 2016, the quarter end that pairs with ERP_STATUS_2016Q3.","full":"The person's in-Australia status at 30 September 2016, the quarter end that pairs with ERP_STATUS_2016Q3. Everything in this panel traces back to border crossings, which ABS scopes narrowly: \"Overseas arrivals and departures (OAD) refer to the recorded arrival or departure of persons through Australian air or sea ports (excluding operational air and ships' crew)\" (ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24). A merchant seafarer or airline crew member working through September 2016 is flagged by CREW_FLAG_FINAL in madip_ge_mig_travellers_2016 and sits outside those counts, so this panel describes their movements poorly.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2016m9","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of September 2016","def":"A single categorical status at 30 September 2016, matched by ERP_STATUS_2016Q3 in the module's quarterly residence table. It carries location only: the state, visa and direction fields for the underlying movements sit in madip_ge_mig_travellers_2016 and none of them reach this column.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","lim":"It says nothing about where in Australia the person was, or on what visa. State of stay, visa subclass and movement direction sit in the yearly traveller tables such as madip_ge_mig_travellers_2016, as STATE, VISA_SUBCLASS and NOM_DIRECTION, and none of that detail survives into a presence flag, so this column cannot support a state-level presence measure.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2017M1","d":"Whether the person was in Australia at 31 January 2017, the month end that closes the southern summer holiday period.","full":"Whether the person was in Australia at 31 January 2017, the month end that closes the southern summer holiday period. January is the mirror image of the December column beside it, with many residents still abroad and many visitors still in the country, so the two together bracket the seasonal high point of the present population. It is a mid-quarter month, which means the migration module offers no residence reading for the same date.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2017m1","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of January 2017","def":"A categorical value for 31 January 2017, column 133 of 240. The item has no published valid-response list, so any recode has to be built from the distinct values found in the extract rather than from the PLIDA data item list.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"It does not say why a person was away. A resident on a January family holiday, a student home between semesters and somebody who has left Australia for good all read the same at this month end, and separating them takes the movement records or the 12/16 month outcome, not the flag.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2017M10","d":"Presence in Australia at 31 October 2017, a status ABS assigns rather than one the traveller reports.","full":"Presence in Australia at 31 October 2017, a status ABS assigns rather than one the traveller reports. No form asks a person whether they were in the country on the last night of October; the value is produced by ordering that person's recorded crossings and reading off where the sequence leaves them. That makes the column a derived statistical determination, with the same standing as ABS category-of-travel coding rather than the standing of a declared field.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2017m10","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of October 2017","def":"A status for 31 October 2017 that ABS determines itself, by ordering that person's recorded crossings. The incoming passenger card collects no field from which the value could be copied.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","lim":"A derived value inherits every error in the sequence that produced it. One unmatched departure early in a person's history can leave every later column on the wrong side, so a single wrong crossing in 2013 can make the October 2017 reading wrong without anything on the row flagging it.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2017M11","d":"In-Australia status at 30 November 2017, filled for every person on the migration table whether or not they crossed a border that year.","full":"In-Australia status at 30 November 2017, filled for every person on the migration table whether or not they crossed a border that year. The panel is a rectangle, so the column exists for people who have never left Australia and for people who had not yet arrived in 2017, and the value distinguishes those two situations only in combination with the rest of the row. November sits just before the December peak, so it is the last month of the year at ordinary travel levels.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2017m11","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of November 2017","def":"A month-end status for 30 November 2017, column 143 of the 240 in this panel. It sits between the September and December quarter ends and has no counterpart in madipge_mig_d_erp_2006_current, which reports only at quarter ends.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"A filled cell is not evidence that anything was observed. Because the rectangle has no gaps, a November 2017 value exists for people with no movement record at all, and taking the column as a record of an observation rather than of a derivation overstates what is known about them.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2017M12","d":"Presence in Australia at 31 December 2017, a quarter end sitting in the middle of the summer visitor season.","full":"Presence in Australia at 31 December 2017, a quarter end sitting in the middle of the summer visitor season. Many of the people flagged present here are visitors who will never become migrants, because ABS counts overseas migrant arrivals as \"Incoming international travellers who stay in Australia for 12 months or more over a 16-month period, who are not currently counted within the population, and are then added to the population\" (ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24). A December present flag is therefore a weak signal of settlement and a strong signal of being in the country.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2017m12","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of December 2017","def":"A categorical value for 31 December 2017, matched by ERP_STATUS_2017Q4. It records presence, and whether the person had been added to the estimated resident population is answered by that quarterly column rather than by this one.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","lim":"It will not identify migrant arrivals. Selecting people present at 31 December 2017 who were absent a year earlier returns holidaymakers and short-stay visitors alongside genuine arrivals, and the addition to the population only happens once the duration test is satisfied months later.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2017M2","d":"The physically present flag for 28 February 2017, a month end that falls a day earlier than its 2016 counterpart.","full":"The physically present flag for 28 February 2017, a month end that falls a day earlier than its 2016 counterpart. February is when the education-driven arrivals for first semester land, so the present population climbs against the resident population without any change in who lives here. Because month ends are not evenly spaced, a February column covers a shorter window of border activity than the months either side of it.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2017m2","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of February 2017","def":"One code per person for 28 February 2017, a month end one day earlier in the calendar than its 2016 counterpart, which fell on 29 February in that leap year. Month ends are the panel's only reference points, and nothing between them is recorded in any column.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"It carries no visa and no reason for travel. A student who arrived for semester one and a tourist who arrived the same week are indistinguishable here, and the visa detail that would separate them sits in VISA and in the yearly traveller tables rather than on this panel.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2017M3","d":"In-Australia status at 31 March 2017, the quarter end matched by ERP_STATUS_2017Q1 in the module's residence table.","full":"In-Australia status at 31 March 2017, the quarter end matched by ERP_STATUS_2017Q1 in the module's residence table. The residence measure is deliberately not about location: ABS defines the estimated resident population as covering \"all people, regardless of their country of citizenship or legal status, who usually live in Australia, with the exception of foreign diplomatic personnel and their families\" (ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24). Someone can therefore be counted in the March 2017 resident population and still be flagged as not present here.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2017m3","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of March 2017","def":"The item holds a location status for 31 March 2017, paired with ERP_STATUS_2017Q1. ABS builds it from Home Affairs crossings alone, which makes it independent of the tax, health and payment products that make up most of the rest of PLIDA.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","lim":"It will not identify a diplomat, and it will not exclude one. Foreign diplomatic personnel and their families are outside the resident population by definition but still cross the border and still appear in a presence panel, so a March 2017 present count is not a filtered version of the quarterly residence count.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2017M4","d":"Presence in Australia at 30 April 2017, one of 240 monthly columns on a table that holds one row per person.","full":"Presence in Australia at 30 April 2017, one of 240 monthly columns on a table that holds one row per person. The panel shape is the thing to plan for: a year of presence means naming twelve columns, and any join to a long-format PLIDA product means reshaping this table before the join rather than after it. April 2017 itself is a quiet travel month with no quarter end and no Census night attached.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2017m4","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of April 2017","def":"A per-person value for 30 April 2017 in a wide panel rather than a long one: the reference date is carried by the column name, not by any field in the row. Renaming or pivoting the column therefore moves the only record of which month the value belongs to.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"One column is not a series and cannot be treated as one. Selecting PP_STATUS_2017M4 alone gives a single night and drops the context that makes it meaningful, and there is nothing in the column itself that records which month it belongs to once it has been renamed in a pipeline.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2017M5","d":"The person's in-Australia status at 31 May 2017, a mid-quarter month with no residence counterpart.","full":"The person's in-Australia status at 31 May 2017, a mid-quarter month with no residence counterpart. Counting present flags across a run of these columns is the standard way to build a months-in-country exposure denominator, which matters when a person is only at risk of using an Australian service while they are in the country. May 2017 is a low-travel month, so it contributes near its maximum to any such count for that year.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2017m5","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of May 2017","def":"A status for 31 May 2017, one of 240 columns that together give a person twenty years of month-end locations across a single row. That layout is what makes counting across columns the natural way to summarise the item.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"An exposure measure built this way is coarse by construction. Each column contributes a whole month or nothing, so a person who was in Australia for 29 of the 31 days of May 2017 but away on the last night contributes zero, and short absences around month ends bias the denominator downwards.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2017M6","d":"In-Australia status at 30 June 2017, the quarter and financial year end matching ERP_STATUS_2017Q2.","full":"In-Australia status at 30 June 2017, the quarter and financial year end matching ERP_STATUS_2017Q2. Presence at a month end is not migration, which ABS settles with a duration test: the 12/16 month rule is \"The method used to measure overseas migration based on traveller duration in or out of Australia for a cumulative 12 months, measured over a 16-month period\" (ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24). A monthly presence panel is the closest thing in PLIDA to the raw material of that test, but it is not the test itself.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2017m6","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of June 2017","def":"A location status for 30 June 2017, the June quarter end matched by ERP_STATUS_2017Q2. It states where a person was and carries no migration outcome; the determination that decides migration is made in the ABS process and is not written back into this panel.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","lim":"Rebuilding the 12/16 month rule from these columns will not reproduce ABS migration outcomes. The rule works on cumulative days from the movement history, not on twelve month-end snapshots, so a count of present months across 2017 and 2018 is an approximation that can fall on the other side of the threshold from the official determination.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2017M7","d":"Presence in Australia at 31 July 2017, in a year with no Census night for the panel to anchor against.","full":"Presence in Australia at 31 July 2017, in a year with no Census night for the panel to anchor against. The table carries Census-night flags only for 2006, 2011, 2016 and 2021, so in the years between them the monthly columns are the only presence readings available. July 2017 falls in the winter school holidays, when resident departures run above their annual average.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2017m7","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of July 2017","def":"A month-end status for 31 July 2017, one of the eight month ends a year with no quarterly residence counterpart. Its weight, PP_WT_2017M7, sits in madipge_mig_d_ppw_2006_current and has to be joined in explicitly.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"There is no Census benchmark for this month to be checked against. Presence readings in 2016 and 2021 can be compared with an independent enumeration, but a 2017 month end stands on the movement records alone, so any coverage problem in those records passes through unexamined.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2017M8","d":"The physically present flag for 31 August 2017, the same calendar month as the 2016 Census but with no Census-night partner column.","full":"The physically present flag for 31 August 2017, the same calendar month as the 2016 Census but with no Census-night partner column. Reading this column beside PP_STATUS_2016M8 gives a clean year-on-year comparison of who was in the country at the end of August, uncontaminated by the enumeration effects that sit around a Census. Both months are mid-quarter, so neither has a residence counterpart.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2017m8","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of August 2017","def":"A single categorical status at 31 August 2017. The table carries PP_CENSUS flags only for 2006, 2011, 2016 and 2021, so in 2017 the monthly columns are the only presence readings available for the person.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"Year-on-year differences in this column mix real change with changes in linkage. The set of people on the migration spine grows as new arrivals link in, so a rise between August 2016 and August 2017 can reflect more linked records rather than more people in the country.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2017M9","d":"The person's in-Australia status at 30 September 2017, the quarter end paired with ERP_STATUS_2017Q3.","full":"The person's in-Australia status at 30 September 2017, the quarter end paired with ERP_STATUS_2017Q3. The aggregate this feeds is an identity rather than a survey estimate: \"Physically present population estimates (PPPE) are calculated as ERP plus total Visitors Temporarily in Australia (VTA) less total Residents Temporarily Overseas (RTO)\" (ABS, Population physically present in Australia). At a quarter end all three terms have published values, which makes September a natural point to check a person-level count against.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2017m9","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of September 2017","def":"Per person, one code for 30 September 2017, the quarter end covered by ERP_STATUS_2017Q3. ABS derives it from sequenced border crossings and releases it in PLIDA only as a person-level status; the aggregate estimates for the same date are published separately.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"A person-level flag cannot be decomposed into the published components. Nothing here says whether a present person is counted as a resident, as a visitor temporarily in Australia, or as neither, so the identity behind the published figure cannot be reassembled from this column alone.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2018M1","d":"Whether the person was in Australia at 31 January 2018, one column in a monthly presence panel that begins in 2006.","full":"Whether the person was in Australia at 31 January 2018, one column in a monthly presence panel that begins in 2006. The value is a location on one night and carries no history with it, so a visitor who arrived on 30 January and a person who has lived in Australia for thirty years read identically. January is the month when the largest share of the people flagged present are short-stay visitors.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2018m1","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of January 2018","def":"One code per person for 31 January 2018. The value is categorical and unordered, so it should be handled as a factor rather than as a 0/1 indicator until the distinct codes in the extract have been checked.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"It does not say how long the person had already been in the country. Time since arrival, and therefore any notion of settlement, has to be recovered by walking back along the row until the presence run breaks, and for someone who arrived before 2006 the panel simply does not go back far enough.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2018M10","d":"Presence in Australia at 31 October 2018, set by the direction of the person's most recent recorded crossing before that night.","full":"Presence in Australia at 31 October 2018, set by the direction of the person's most recent recorded crossing before that night. If the last movement was an arrival the person reads as present, and if it was a departure they read as away, which is why the accuracy of the column depends entirely on the crossings before it rather than on anything in October. The month itself is unremarkable, sitting between the quarter ends of September and December.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2018m10","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of October 2018","def":"A month-end status for 31 October 2018, set by the direction of the last crossing recorded before that night. The value is carried forward from whenever that crossing happened and changes only when the next one is recorded.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","lim":"It does not record when the crossing that set it happened. A person present at 31 October 2018 may have arrived that week or a decade earlier, and recovering the date means going back to the movement tables, so this column cannot support any measure that depends on recency of arrival.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2018M11","d":"In-Australia status at 30 November 2018, most informative when read against the columns either side of it.","full":"In-Australia status at 30 November 2018, most informative when read against the columns either side of it. A change between the October and November flags marks a crossing somewhere in November, and an unchanged pair rules out only crossings that straddled a month end. November 2018 is the last full month before the December peak, so it is a reasonable baseline for the summer months that follow it.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2018m11","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of November 2018","def":"A categorical value for 30 November 2018. The panel runs continuously from 2006M1 with no gaps in the monthly sequence, so PP_STATUS_2018M10 and PP_STATUS_2018M12 always exist for the same person.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"A change between two adjacent columns is a lower bound on travel, not a count of it. Somebody who left and returned twice within November 2018 shows no change at all, so treating transitions in this panel as a trip count will understate travel for exactly the people who travel most.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2018M12","d":"Presence in Australia at 31 December 2018, a quarter end at the height of the summer travel season.","full":"Presence in Australia at 31 December 2018, a quarter end at the height of the summer travel season. The measure it is most often mistaken for is defined on residence, not location: \"The official measure of the population of Australia is based on the concept of usual residence\" (ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24). In December that gap is at its widest, because the country holds an unusual number of people who do not live here and is missing an unusual number of people who do.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2018m12","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of December 2018","def":"One code per person for 31 December 2018, the last of the four 2018 quarter-end columns. The PLIDA data item list publishes no categories for the item and draws no distinction between one column's categories and another's, so the codes have to be tabulated from the extract.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","lim":"December readings will not average out against each other across years. Every December column in the panel is displaced in the same direction by the same seasonal pattern, so a study using only quarter ends inherits a systematic summer bias rather than noise that cancels.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2018M2","d":"The physically present flag for 28 February 2018, a month end well inside the panel's pre-pandemic stretch.","full":"The physically present flag for 28 February 2018, a month end well inside the panel's pre-pandemic stretch. Because the panel starts at 2006M1 and is complete for everyone on the table, a person who first arrived in Australia after February 2018 still has a value in this column, and it reflects their absence rather than any event. That structural feature matters more in the early columns than the late ones, but it never disappears.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2018m2","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of February 2018","def":"The item holds a status for 28 February 2018, joined to the rest of the migration module on SYNTHETIC_AEUID rather than on any Home Affairs identifier. A monthly flag is settled the moment the crossings are in, while the migration measure beside it is not: the 12/16 month rule is \"The method used to measure overseas migration based on traveller duration in or out of Australia for a cumulative 12 months, measured over a 16-month period\" (ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24). Presence in March 2018 was known in April 2018; whether the same person was a migrant took until well into 2019 to determine.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2018m3","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of March 2018","def":"A per-person value for 31 March 2018, one of the four columns a year with a same-date entry in madipge_mig_d_erp_2006_current. Neither item has a published code list, so a March quarter comparison across the two tables needs both category sets tabulated from the extract first.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","lim":"The timeliness of this column does not extend to the residence column beside it. Quarterly ERP status for recent periods rests on modelled migration outcomes until the 16-month follow-up completes, so a study pairing March presence with March residence is combining a settled value with a provisional one.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2018M4","d":"Presence in Australia at 30 April 2018, a settled month that the border-affected months later in the panel are usually compared against.","full":"Presence in Australia at 30 April 2018, a settled month that the border-affected months later in the panel are usually compared against. Travel regimes change the meaning of these columns, so an April 2018 reading and an April 2020 reading are not two draws from the same process. Nothing in the column names signals that break, which is why the calendar month attached to each column has to be carried through any analysis.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/overseas-arrivals-and-departures-australia/dec-2020","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2018m4","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of April 2018","def":"A status for 30 April 2018 built from movement records rather than from any Australian service interaction. The column is therefore populated for people who appear in no other PLIDA product that month.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/overseas-arrivals-and-departures-australia/dec-2020","lim":"It cannot warn you that the columns after it are not comparable with it. The panel presents 240 identically shaped columns with no marker for the 2020 border closure, so a model pooling all of them treats a month of open borders and a month of closed borders as the same kind of observation.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2018M5","d":"The person's in-Australia status at 31 May 2018, recorded monthly where most PLIDA products report quarterly or annually.","full":"The person's in-Australia status at 31 May 2018, recorded monthly where most PLIDA products report quarterly or annually. That finer grain is the main reason to use the presence panel at all, since it can place a person in or out of the country at a month end that no other product observes. It also forces a choice of convention when the presence flag is joined to a quarterly or financial year measure.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2018m5","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of May 2018","def":"A location status for 31 May 2018, recorded monthly where the module's residence table reports quarterly and the traveller tables report one reference movement at a time. The three grains sit in the same module and are joined on the same person key.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"The monthly grain is finer than the accuracy behind it. Presence is derived from crossings whose dates are recorded to the day, but a person whose record has a missing return leg will be wrong for every month until the next observed crossing, so the monthly resolution can suggest a precision the underlying sequence does not have.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2018M6","d":"In-Australia status at 30 June 2018, the quarter and financial year end matched by ERP_STATUS_2018Q2.","full":"In-Australia status at 30 June 2018, the quarter and financial year end matched by ERP_STATUS_2018Q2. The border events that decide the value are air and sea crossings only: \"Overseas arrivals and departures (OAD) refer to the recorded arrival or departure of persons through Australian air or sea ports (excluding operational air and ships' crew)\" (ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24). A 30 June reading is the one most often used to align presence with financial year measures such as income and tax records.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2018m6","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of June 2018","def":"A month-end status for 30 June 2018, both the June quarter end matched by ERP_STATUS_2018Q2 and the close of the 2017-18 financial year. This makes it independent of the tax, health and payment records elsewhere in PLIDA, so it can be used to check them: somebody with Medicare claims in a month the panel says they were overseas is a discrepancy worth investigating. July 2018 opens a financial year, which is where many of those administrative series restart.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2018m7","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of July 2018","def":"A single categorical status at 31 July 2018, derived from air and sea border crossings only. Plenty of people who were present in July 2018 generated no record in any other PLIDA product that month, so agreement between silence in the service data and a not-present flag here proves nothing about either.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2018M8","d":"The physically present flag for 31 August 2018, a monthly summary of the movements the 2018 traveller table holds one by one.","full":"The physically present flag for 31 August 2018, a monthly summary of the movements the 2018 traveller table holds one by one. The two live in the same module and answer different questions: madip_ge_mig_travellers_2018 has a row per reference movement with its direction, visa and category of travel, while this panel has a column per month with only the resulting location. Working from the movement table upwards gives more detail, and working from this panel across gives a ready-made timeline.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2018m8","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of August 2018","def":"Per person, one code for 31 August 2018, summarising at a single date the movements that madip_ge_mig_travellers_2018 holds one row at a time. The yearly tables carry a reference movement per person per period rather than every crossing, so a person can have one traveller row for 2018 and a presence panel that changes several times across the year without either being wrong.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2018M9","d":"The person's in-Australia status at 30 September 2018, the quarter end paired with ERP_STATUS_2018Q3.","full":"The person's in-Australia status at 30 September 2018, the quarter end paired with ERP_STATUS_2018Q3. Being here and joining the population are different events, and ABS separates them: overseas migrant arrivals are \"Incoming international travellers who stay in Australia for 12 months or more over a 16-month period, who are not currently counted within the population, and are then added to the population\" (ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24). Somebody who arrived in September 2018 and stayed would be present in this column immediately and added to the population much later.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2018m9","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of September 2018","def":"A status for 30 September 2018, matched by ERP_STATUS_2018Q3.
