January 2020 was unrestricted too, with the first measures coming in from 1 February 2020, so the break in this panel falls after both of them.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2019m1","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of January 2019","def":"The item holds a location status for 31 January 2019, column 157 of 240. It is location only: visa, citizenship and country of birth for the same person sit in the yearly traveller tables and in the VISA dataset.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"It cannot be used as a pre-period without choosing where the pre-period stops. Restrictions came in progressively rather than on one day, so a difference-in-differences design anchored on January 2019 has to justify which later months count as treated, and the panel offers no marker to do that with.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2019M10","d":"Presence in Australia at 31 October 2019, with the visitor stock building towards a summer that arrived normally.","full":"Presence in Australia at 31 October 2019, with the visitor stock building towards a summer that arrived normally. Read forward from this column and the panel behaves as it has since 2006 for another four months before the pattern breaks. Read back from it and October 2019 is indistinguishable from October 2018 or October 2017, which is what makes the pre-pandemic part of the panel usable as a single regime.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2019m10","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of October 2019","def":"A categorical value for 31 October 2019 on a table with one row per person and no time dimension in the rows. Any analysis organised by month needs the table pivoted long before the value can be used as a series.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"Stability across pre-pandemic Octobers is not evidence that the underlying population is stable. The set of people linked into the migration table grows over time, so a column can look unchanged year on year while the composition behind it shifts, and this panel carries nothing that would show the difference.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2019M11","d":"In-Australia status at 30 November 2019, the last November in the panel with an ordinary visitor population.","full":"In-Australia status at 30 November 2019, the last November in the panel with an ordinary visitor population. The people flagged present here include a large stock of short-stay visitors, and that stock is what drained away over 2020 once arrivals stopped replacing departures. Comparing this column with PP_STATUS_2020M10 or PP_STATUS_2020M11 shows the drain rather than any change in who lives in Australia.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/overseas-arrivals-and-departures-australia/dec-2020","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2019m11","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of November 2019","def":"One code per person for 30 November 2019. Its weight, PP_WT_2019M11, is held in madipge_mig_d_ppw_2006_current, and the nearest quarterly column, ERP_STATUS_2019Q4, covers 31 December rather than this date.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/overseas-arrivals-and-departures-australia/dec-2020","lim":"It cannot attribute a later fall in presence to any cause. The panel records that fewer people were in the country, not whether that was because visitors left, because arrivals were blocked, or because residents went overseas, and separating those requires the movement direction held in the traveller tables.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2019M12","d":"Presence in Australia at 31 December 2019, the final undisrupted summer peak the panel records.","full":"Presence in Australia at 31 December 2019, the final undisrupted summer peak the panel records. It is a quarter end, so ERP_STATUS_2019Q4 covers the same date, and the two diverge here about as much as they ever do because \"The population usually resident is less influenced by seasonality and is usually slightly higher than the population present\" (ABS, Population physically present in Australia). Every December column after this one reflects a closed or restricted border rather than the ordinary summer pattern.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2019m12","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of December 2019","def":"The item holds a status for 31 December 2019, matched by ERP_STATUS_2019Q4 and the last December quarter end in the panel before border restrictions. It states where a person was, not how long they had been there.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"It is the wrong benchmark for a seasonally naive comparison. Setting December 2019 against December 2020 attributes the whole difference to the border closure when part of it is the summer swing that the 2020 column could not have, so the comparison overstates the closure effect on residents.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2019M2","d":"The physically present flag for 28 February 2019, the base month against which February 2020 is normally read.","full":"The physically present flag for 28 February 2019, the base month against which February 2020 is normally read. ABS reports pandemic-period travel as year-on-year comparisons against the matching 2019 month, and this panel supports the same approach at person level. February 2019 is the last February in the panel with a full inbound student and visitor season behind it.","dsrc":"ABS, Further steep declines in overseas travel in April","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/further-steep-declines-overseas-travel-april","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2019m2","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of February 2019","def":"A per-person value for 28 February 2019, one of the eight month ends a year with no entry in madipge_mig_d_erp_2006_current. February is the shortest reference gap in the panel, at 28 days from the January column in non-leap years.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Further steep declines in overseas travel in April","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/further-steep-declines-overseas-travel-april","lim":"A person-level comparison with 2020 will not match published movement counts. ABS year-on-year figures count crossings over a whole month, while this column counts people in the country on one night, so the two series can move by very different amounts for the same underlying change.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2019M3","d":"In-Australia status at 31 March 2019, the quarter end falling exactly one year before the border closed.","full":"In-Australia status at 31 March 2019, the quarter end falling exactly one year before the border closed. Its value comes from the ordinary operation of the movement collection, which ABS scopes as \"the recorded arrival or departure of persons through Australian air or sea ports (excluding operational air and ships' crew)\" (ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24). The same collection kept running through 2020, which is why the panel continues without a break even as what it records changes completely.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2019m3","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of March 2019","def":"A status for 31 March 2019, matched by ERP_STATUS_2019Q1. The column definition is the same for every month of the panel, and the derivation did not change when travel conditions did.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","lim":"Continuity of the column is not continuity of meaning. The panel gives March 2019 and March 2020 the same shape and the same derivation, but the population able to cross the border differs between them, so an unchanged column definition hides a change in what the value describes.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2019M4","d":"Presence in Australia at 30 April 2019, the month ABS uses as the comparison base for April 2020.","full":"Presence in Australia at 30 April 2019, the month ABS uses as the comparison base for April 2020. ABS reported that \"COVID-19 travel restrictions saw a 99 per cent decrease in overseas arrivals to Australia in April 2020, compared with April 2019\" (ABS, Further steep declines in overseas travel in April), which makes this column the before side of the sharpest break in the whole panel. It is a mid-quarter month, so no residence reading exists for the same date on either side of the comparison.","dsrc":"ABS, Further steep declines in overseas travel in April","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/further-steep-declines-overseas-travel-april","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2019m4","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of April 2019","def":"A location status for 30 April 2019, a mid-quarter month end with no matching column in the module's quarterly residence table. Everything this module records about where the person was in April 2019 is in this one column.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Further steep declines in overseas travel in April","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/further-steep-declines-overseas-travel-april","lim":"A 99 per cent fall in arrivals does not translate into a comparable fall in this column. Presence is a stock and arrivals are a flow, so the people already in Australia in April 2020 stayed flagged present while the inbound flow that would have replaced them stopped, and the panel moves far less than the movement statistics do.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2019M5","d":"The person's in-Australia status at 31 May 2019, in the last full year of unrestricted travel the panel covers.","full":"The person's in-Australia status at 31 May 2019, in the last full year of unrestricted travel the panel covers. Because the visitor stock was at ordinary levels, the difference between this column and the resident population is close to the long-run average, which makes May 2019 a defensible reference month for anyone calibrating a presence-based measure. There is no quarter end and no Census night attached to it.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2019m5","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of May 2019","def":"A month-end status for 31 May 2019 that is derived rather than collected. ABS produces it from the movement history and it arrives in PLIDA already determined, with no downstream agency contributing to the value.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"Calibrating on a normal month does not make the calibration hold later. The relationship between people flagged present and the published present population depends on the mix of residents and visitors, and that mix changed sharply from March 2020, so a ratio fitted on May 2019 will not carry into the closed-border months.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2019M6","d":"In-Australia status at 30 June 2019, closing the last complete pre-pandemic financial year in the panel.","full":"In-Australia status at 30 June 2019, closing the last complete pre-pandemic financial year in the panel. At a quarter end all the terms of the published identity are available: \"Physically present population estimates (PPPE) are calculated as ERP plus total Visitors Temporarily in Australia (VTA) less total Residents Temporarily Overseas (RTO)\" (ABS, Population physically present in Australia). That makes June 2019 the most checkable month in the pre-pandemic part of the panel.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2019m6","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of June 2019","def":"A single categorical status at 30 June 2019, the June quarter end matched by ERP_STATUS_2019Q2 and the close of the 2018-19 financial year. Quarter-end columns are the only ones whose reference date is also covered by published ABS present-population estimates.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"Agreement with a published quarterly figure would not validate the column for other months. The check only covers quarter ends, and eight months in every year have no published present population to be compared against, so most of the panel is unverifiable against ABS output.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2019M7","d":"Presence in Australia at 31 July 2019, opening a financial year the border closure would cut in half.","full":"Presence in Australia at 31 July 2019, opening a financial year the border closure would cut in half. The first eight months of 2019-20 look like any other year in this panel and the last four do not, so a measure aggregated over that financial year mixes two regimes. Anyone building an annual presence measure from monthly columns should treat 2019-20 as the year where that aggregation stops being safe.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/overseas-arrivals-and-departures-australia/dec-2020","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2019m7","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of July 2019","def":"Per person, one code for 31 July 2019, the first month end of the 2019-20 financial year in the panel. Financial year aggregations built from these columns are the analyst's construction, since the item has no annual form.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/overseas-arrivals-and-departures-australia/dec-2020","lim":"It cannot flag the point where the year it belongs to stops being homogeneous. An annual count of present months for 2019-20 returns a single number that conceals a structural break in March 2020, and nothing in this column or its neighbours records that the break happened.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2019M8","d":"The physically present flag for 31 August 2019, midway between the 2016 and 2021 Census anchors on this table.","full":"The physically present flag for 31 August 2019, midway between the 2016 and 2021 Census anchors on this table. The Census-night columns are the only readings in the module that can be checked against an independent count of who was in the country, and ABS makes that link explicit: \"Census count by place of enumeration is a measure of the population present in Australia on Census night\" (ABS, Population physically present in Australia). August 2019 has no such anchor, so it rests entirely on the movement records.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2019m8","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of August 2019","def":"A status for 31 August 2019 resting on border records alone, with no independent count behind it. The only columns on this table with an external benchmark are the four PP_CENSUS flags.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"It offers no way to detect a person who is in the country without a matching movement record. Somebody who overstayed, or whose arrival failed to link to the spine, is invisible to this column in the same way as somebody genuinely overseas, and only a Census year gives an independent count that could reveal the gap.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2019M9","d":"The person's in-Australia status at 30 September 2019, a quarter end whose migration follow-up window ran into 2021.","full":"The person's in-Australia status at 30 September 2019, a quarter end whose migration follow-up window ran into 2021. The 12/16 month rule is \"The method used to measure overseas migration based on traveller duration in or out of Australia for a cumulative 12 months, measured over a 16-month period\" (ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24), so the 16 months after this date cover the border closure. Somebody who left Australia in late 2019 for a normal trip could be classified as an emigrant because the closure kept them out.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2019m9","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of September 2019","def":"A month-end status for 30 September 2019, column 165 of 240 and the last September quarter end in the panel before the border closed. Like every other column here it is a categorical location status with no published code list.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Migration methodology, 2023-24 financial year","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/overseas-migration-methodology/2023-24","lim":"It does not distinguish an intended absence from an enforced one. The presence flags after September 2019 record where people were, not whether they could return, so a person stranded abroad and a person who chose to emigrate leave the same trace across the following columns.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2020M1","d":"Whether the person was in Australia at 31 January 2020, the last month end before COVID-19 travel restrictions began.","full":"Whether the person was in Australia at 31 January 2020, the last month end before COVID-19 travel restrictions began. ABS records that restrictions were \"progressively put in place by the Australian Government from the beginning of February due to the outbreak of COVID-19\" (ABS, Further steep declines in overseas travel in April), which places this column on the untreated side of the break by a single day. It is a mid-quarter month, so the residence table offers no matching reading.","dsrc":"ABS, Further steep declines in overseas travel in April","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/further-steep-declines-overseas-travel-april","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2020m1","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of January 2020","def":"A per-person value for 31 January 2020, column 169 of 240. The derivation is unchanged from the earlier columns: ABS sequences the recorded crossings and reads off the resulting location.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Further steep declines in overseas travel in April","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/further-steep-declines-overseas-travel-april","lim":"It cannot identify who was about to be affected by the restrictions. The early measures applied on the basis of recent travel history rather than to everyone, and this column carries no country of embarkation and no travel history, so the exposed group cannot be selected from the panel alone.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2020M10","d":"Presence in Australia at 31 October 2020, seven months into the closed border.","full":"Presence in Australia at 31 October 2020, seven months into the closed border. By this point the stock of short-stay visitors who were in the country in March had largely departed without being replaced, so the people flagged present are much closer to the resident population than in any pre-pandemic October. The gap between this column and ERP status is therefore unusually small, which is a feature of the regime and not a sign that the two measures agree.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/overseas-arrivals-and-departures-australia/dec-2020","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2020m10","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of October 2020","def":"Per person, one code for 31 October 2020, column 178 of 240. It is one of the eight mid-quarter month ends a year, so nothing in madipge_mig_d_erp_2006_current covers the same date.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/overseas-arrivals-and-departures-australia/dec-2020","lim":"It cannot separate a visitor who left from a visitor whose record simply stops. Departures were recorded throughout 2020, but a person whose last movement was an unmatched exit reads as absent for the rest of the panel, and October 2020 is the point where those two explanations for an absent flag are hardest to tell apart.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2020M11","d":"In-Australia status at 30 November 2020, with the pre-closure visitor stock largely gone.","full":"In-Australia status at 30 November 2020, with the pre-closure visitor stock largely gone. In an ordinary year the November column would be rising towards the summer peak, and in 2020 there was no build-up to record, so the seasonal shape that every earlier November in the panel shows is simply absent. Set against PP_STATUS_2019M11 the difference is almost entirely visitors rather than residents.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/overseas-arrivals-and-departures-australia/dec-2020","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2020m11","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of November 2020","def":"A status for 30 November 2020 produced for every person on the migration table, including those whose last recorded crossing was years earlier. The column is filled regardless of whether the person had any border activity in 2020.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/overseas-arrivals-and-departures-australia/dec-2020","lim":"A fall in the number of people flagged present is not a fall in the Australian population. The people who disappeared from this column over 2020 were mostly never counted in the resident population to begin with, so reading the drop as population loss confuses the visitor term of the published identity with the resident term.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2020M12","d":"Presence in Australia at 31 December 2020, a quarter end at which the usual summer peak did not happen.","full":"Presence in Australia at 31 December 2020, a quarter end at which the usual summer peak did not happen. ABS reported that \"97% of visitor arrivals in 2020 occurred prior to travel restrictions implemented by the Australian Government on 20 March 2020\" (ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020), so the visitors who normally inflate a December column were not in the country. Residents who would ordinarily have been overseas for the holidays were also here, which pushes the present and resident measures unusually close together.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/overseas-arrivals-and-departures-australia/dec-2020","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2020m12","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of December 2020","def":"A month-end status for 31 December 2020, matched by ERP_STATUS_2020Q4. Both columns are derived from the same movement records, but the residence column applies the ABS duration rules for migration and this one does not.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/overseas-arrivals-and-departures-australia/dec-2020","lim":"Close agreement with ERP_STATUS_2020Q4 must not be generalised. The two measures converged in December 2020 because both the visitor and the residents-abroad terms collapsed at once, and taking that as evidence that presence is a usable proxy for residence will fail on every other December in the panel.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2020M2","d":"The physically present flag for 29 February 2020, the first month end under COVID-19 travel restrictions.","full":"The physically present flag for 29 February 2020, the first month end under COVID-19 travel restrictions. ABS describes those measures as \"progressively put in place by the Australian Government from the beginning of February due to the outbreak of COVID-19\" (ABS, Further steep declines in overseas travel in April), so this column covers a partial regime rather than either the open border of January or the closed border from late March. Most people flagged present here had entered Australia before any restriction applied.","dsrc":"ABS, Further steep declines in overseas travel in April","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/further-steep-declines-overseas-travel-april","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2020m2","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of February 2020","def":"A status for 29 February 2020, a leap-year month end. The panel keeps its monthly cadence through 2020 with no change of definition, so this column is built the same way as PP_STATUS_2016M2 even though the two describe very different conditions.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Further steep declines in overseas travel in April","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/further-steep-declines-overseas-travel-april","lim":"Treating February 2020 as either a clean before or a clean after period will misstate the effect being measured. Restrictions were partial through the month, so this column is a mixture, and assigning it to one side of a border-closure comparison attributes part of the transition to the wrong regime.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2020M3","d":"In-Australia status at 31 March 2020, eleven days after the border closed and at the quarter end covered by ERP_STATUS_2020Q1.","full":"In-Australia status at 31 March 2020, eleven days after the border closed and at the quarter end covered by ERP_STATUS_2020Q1. ABS states that \"From 20 March 2020, all overseas travel was banned, with few exceptions\" (ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020), so this column captures the population that happened to be in the country when movement stopped. It holds both residents who had rushed home and visitors who had not yet left.","dsrc":"ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/overseas-arrivals-and-departures-australia/dec-2020","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2020m3","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of March 2020","def":"A location status for 31 March 2020, matched by ERP_STATUS_2020Q1. The value depends only on the crossings recorded before that night, so the collapse in crossing volumes during March reaches the column through the movement history rather than through any change of method.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia, December 2020","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/overseas-arrivals-and-departures-australia/dec-2020","lim":"A present flag in March 2020 does not mean the person intended to be in Australia, and an absent flag does not mean they intended to be away. The column records location on one night in a month when many people's location was decided by flight cancellations and entry rules, so any reading of it as revealed preference is wrong for this month in particular.","where":["madipge-mig-d-pp-2006-current / madipge_mig_d_pp_2006_current"]},{"n":"PP_STATUS_2020M4","d":"Presence in Australia at 30 April 2020, the first full month end with the border closed.","full":"Presence in Australia at 30 April 2020, the first full month end with the border closed. ABS reported that \"COVID-19 travel restrictions saw a 99 per cent decrease in overseas arrivals to Australia in April 2020, compared with April 2019\" (ABS, Further steep declines in overseas travel in April), and of the roughly 22,000 arrivals that month more than two thirds were Australian citizens returning. Almost nobody changed presence status in April 2020, so the column is close to a copy of the March one.","dsrc":"ABS, Further steep declines in overseas travel in April","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/further-steep-declines-overseas-travel-april","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present status at end of 2020m4","k":"Physically present in Australia status, end of April 2020","def":"A month-end status for 30 April 2020. July does not close a quarter, so it has no counterpart in the quarterly ERP status columns of madipge_mig_d_erp_2006_current and cannot be matched to a published quarterly figure. 2009 sits well inside the settled part of the series: the 16-month follow-up window that the 12 out of 16 month rule needs for net overseas migration closed long ago, so the migration component of the population total this weight scales to is no longer preliminary.","dsrc":"ABS, 'Population physically present in Australia', article released 18 June 2026; ABS, PLIDA data and legislation (Net Overseas Migration Traveller data)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present weight at end of 2009m7","k":"Physically present population weight (end of July 2009)","def":"A numeric weight for one month, one column per month, 240 columns from January 2006 to December 2025 in madipge_mig_d_ppw_2006_current, matching the status columns in the companion table one for one. PP_STATUS_2009M8 on the companion table says whether the person was in the country at that month end, and this column says how much that answer counts for. The ABS defines that population as the one \"counted in a certain area or country at a given point in time, regardless of where they usually live\" (Population physically present in Australia). August 2009 falls between Census years, so the nearest independent presence count on the row is PP_CENSUS_2011, two years after this month end, while the closest quarterly ERP status is ERP_STATUS_2009Q3, struck a month later at the end of September.","dsrc":"ABS, Population physically present in Australia","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physically present weight at end of 2009m8","k":"Physically present population weight, end of August 2009","def":"A non-negative number held once per person per month, on the scale of people rather than days or dollars. Fully enumerated records sit at one, since all permanent arrivals and all arrivals of a year or more have always been fully enumerated and every departure has been since July 2007, while a record drawn from the short-term arrival sample carries a larger factor. At the roughly 5 per cent overall rate that ran from July 2007 to April 2020 that factor is of the order of twenty, but the sample is a fixed skip with a threshold set by country of citizenship, so individual weights sit well above and well below that average. The ABS builds that count as PPPE = ERP + VTA - RTO from overseas arrivals and departures records and publishes it quarterly from the December quarter 2006 to the December quarter 2025, so the nearest published counterpart to April 2023 is the quarter end carried by PP_WT_2023M6.","p":"2006 to 2023","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Bureau of Statistics, Population physically present in Australia","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/population-physically-present-australia","lim":"This column is more likely than an older one to move between PLIDA vintages. The table runs one row per person and 240 monthly columns, PP_WT_2006M1 through PP_WT_2025M12, so a person's series reads across the row rather than down the file, and this is column 209. The ABS compiles the physically present population by reference quarter, so May sits inside the June quarter 2023 with no published quarterly figure of its own, and PP_WT_2023M6 is the column that falls on one. ERP_STATUS_2023Q2 in madipge_mig_d_erp_2006_current covers the same quarter, so a person's usual-residence status can be set beside their May 2023 presence weight.
